trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for flat attribute edits. All called APIs are documented: constructor, next_tag(), get_attribute_names_with_prefix(), remove_attribute(), and get_updated_html(). The loop follows the documented scan/mutate/readback pattern, handles null from the prefix method, and relies on documented case-insensitive attribute matching and tag/comment behavior.

Same implementation as trial-1. Uses only documented Tag Processor APIs, no _doing_it_wrong records, no structural parser or serialization misuse, and correctly uses the returned lowercase attribute names as removal targets before get_updated_html().

Same implementation as trial-1. Fully aligned with the rendered docs: byte-preserving Tag Processor, next_tag() token walk over openers, prefix-based attribute discovery, remove_attribute(), and get_updated_html().

failure_analysis: No failed hidden cases occurred: all three trials passed 7/7 with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well here. The Tag Processor heading "Which processor should I use?" explicitly recommends the Tag Processor for flat attribute/class edits and byte-precise preservation, which led subjects away from WP_HTML_Processor. The "Usage" and "Modifying HTML attributes for a found tag" sections establish the correct pattern: construct, next_tag(), mutate attributes, then get_updated_html(). The get_attribute_names_with_prefix() section documents lowercase returned names and case-insensitive matching, which explains success on uppercase source attributes. The next_tag() section states comments/raw-text tag-like content is not matched and incomplete trailing tags are not modified, covering the main edge cases. The HTML Processor serialization docs also warn that serialize()/normalize() are not the way to retrieve queued mutations, preventing a common wrong solution. Near-miss: get_attribute_names_with_prefix() does not explicitly say that a matched tag with no matching attributes returns an empty array rather than null; the candidates' foreach-safe code avoided depending on that ambiguity.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say array|null and show null after no tag is matched, but do not explicitly describe the matched-opener/no-prefix-matches case.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State that it returns a possibly empty array when currently matched on an opener, and null only when no tag opener is currently matched or the current token is not an opener.

doc_gaps.problem: The public description is sparse and does not state that attribute-name lookup is ASCII case-insensitive/lowercased, which matters when feeding it names discovered from differently cased source attributes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document that the requested name is matched case-insensitively against HTML attribute names, and that lowercase names returned by get_attribute_names_with_prefix() are valid inputs to remove_attribute().

doc_gaps.problem: The prefix-discovery method and mutation methods are documented separately, so the intended batch-attribute workflow is implied rather than explicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short cross-reference noting that the returned attribute names may be passed to get_attribute(), set_attribute(), or remove_attribute() while processing the current tag.
